title: Baga massacre by Boko Haram
description: Boko Haram attacked Baga and Doron Baga in early January 2015, beginning on January 3. Satellite imagery showed widespread destruction, and witnesses described mass killings. Reported tolls ranged from an official figure around 150, including fighters, to local estimates as high as 2,000; the final number remains uncertain.

review.note: 2,000 was an upper estimate from local accounts, not a confirmed Amnesty body count; government put deaths including fighters at about 150. Satellite destruction cannot by itself resolve deaths. January 3 is campaign start, not a single-day total.

sources.name: Amnesty International, satellite and witness evidence

title: Charlie Hebdo shooting
description: Gunmen attacked Charlie Hebdo's Paris office on January 7, 2015, killing 12 people, including journalists and police officers. The Kouachi brothers were killed by police two days later. Separate linked attacks killed five more people, bringing the January 7-9 victim total to 17.
sources: Committee to Protect Journalists, attack report

title: DusitD2 complex attack
description: Al-Shabaab attacked the DusitD2 hotel and business complex in Nairobi on January 15, 2019. Twenty-one victims were killed. Kenyan authorities said all five attackers also died. The toll of 21 excludes the attackers.

title: Brumadinho dam disaster
description: Vale's Corrego do Feijao tailings dam collapsed at Brumadinho, Brazil, on January 25, 2019, killing 270 people. Local authorities and victims' families commemorate 272 victims when two unborn children are included. Identification and recovery of victims continued for years after the collapse.

title: Kabul ambulance bombing
description: On January 27, 2018, a Taliban attacker detonated explosives carried in an ambulance in central Kabul. Afghanistan's interior minister reported the next day that 103 people had been killed and 235 wounded.

title: Meinong (Kaohsiung) earthquake
description: An earthquake centred near Meinong in southern Taiwan struck at 19:57 UTC on February 5, 2016, or early February 6 locally. It caused severe building collapses in Tainan. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration records 117 deaths.
sources: Taiwan Central Weather Administration, event record
National Center for Research on Earthquake Engineering, study

title: Parkland School Shooting
description: On February 14, 2018, a gunman killed 17 people and wounded 17 others at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida.

title: Pulwama attack
description: A Jaish-e-Mohammed suicide bomber attacked a convoy of Indian paramilitary police in Pulwama on February 14, 2019, killing 40 security personnel. The attack was followed by Indian airstrikes at Balakot and an aerial confrontation between India and Pakistan.

title: South Sudan famine declared
description: Famine was declared in South Sudan's Leer and Mayendit counties on February 20, 2017. UN agencies reported about 100,000 people facing starvation and one million more on the brink of famine. Famine conditions eased by June following increased assistance, while severe food insecurity persisted.

review.note: February 20 is the supported declaration date, not famine onset. UN sources substantiate Leer/Mayendit, roughly 100,000 facing starvation, 4.9 million severely food insecure and one million near famine; June 21 reports famine easing but worsening nationwide hunger. They do not establish an event-specific 20,000 excess-death estimate. Famine classification mortality thresholds cannot be converted into that annual toll.

sources.name: UN Secretary-General report on South Sudan

title: Severnaya coal mine explosions, Vorkuta
description: Methane explosions at the Severnaya mine in Vorkuta on February 25, 2016 killed four miners and trapped 26 others, who were subsequently presumed dead. A third explosion on February 28 killed five rescuers and another miner, bringing the toll to 36.

title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crash
description: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 flying from Addis Ababa to Nairobi, crashed near Bishoftu on March 10, 2019, about six minutes after takeoff. All 157 people aboard died.

title: Cyclone Idai
description: Cyclone Idai made landfall near the port city of Beira in central Mozambique on the night of 14-15 March 2019, bringing torrential rains and winds of up to 175 km/h that caused the Buzi and Pungwe rivers to burst their banks. More than 1,500 people died across Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Madagascar, with the toll later confirmed at 1,593, and more than 2,000 people were reported missing. Hundreds of thousands were left stranded in floodwater, and the United Nations called it one of the worst weather-related disasters to hit the Southern Hemisphere.

review.note: Landfall near Beira March 14-15 established. Claimed confirmed 1,593 and 2,000 missing not established. WHO gives 603 for Mozambique; an EM-DAT-based study gives 1,234 storm deaths. Need consistent multinational period and missing-versus-dead accounting before replacement.

sources.name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Science

title: Christchurch Mosque Shootings
description: A gunman attacked the Al Noor Mosque and Linwood Islamic Centre in Christchurch, New Zealand, on March 15, 2019, killing 51 people.

title: Peru floods and mudslides
description: Coastal El Nino conditions caused severe floods and mudslides in Peru during 2016-2017. Peru's meteorological agency reports 162 deaths and nearly 1.5 million people affected. The disaster spanned several months rather than beginning on March 20.

review.note: SENAMHI supports 162 deaths and nearly 1.5 million affected for the coastal El Nino disaster, formally December 2016-May 2017. March 20 is a publication date for a much earlier 75-death report, not the event onset. RPP attributes 162 to an August INDECI report. The claimed EM-DAT 177 and homeless scope were not independently established. Date remains unresolved even after replacing the prose.

title: Brussels airport and metro bombings
description: Suicide bombings struck Brussels Airport and Maalbeek metro station on March 22, 2016. Thirty-two victims died in the attacks. In 2023, the court recognized three later deaths as attributable to the attacks, bringing the official victim toll to 35.

title: Ogossagou massacre
description: Armed men attacked the Fulani part of Ogossagou village in central Mali at about 05:00 on March 23, 2019. A UN investigation concluded that at least 157 people were killed. It identified most attackers as traditional hunters, accompanied by men in military and civilian clothing.

title: Kemerovo shopping mall fire
description: A fire at the Winter Cherry shopping and entertainment complex in Kemerovo, Russia, on March 25, 2018 killed 60 people, including children. Later investigations found serious fire-safety failures.

title: Lahore Easter park bombing
description: A suicide bombing struck Lahore's Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park on Easter Sunday, March 27, 2016. Jamaat-ul-Ahrar claimed responsibility and said it targeted Christians. Published death totals differ, including reports of victims dying later from injuries.

review.note: Date, location and attack identity are supported. PIPS's annual report gives at least 74 deaths including 29 children and over 233 injuries. SATP's incident prose says 74, its table 75, and its April 21 entry reports a later victim raising the toll to 78. These inconsistencies do not establish a final 75 or a final child/injury breakdown. Christian targeting was the attackers' stated intent, not evidence that every victim was Christian.

title: Mocoa mudslide, Colombia
description: Floodwater and debris swept through Mocoa in Colombia's Putumayo department on the night of March 31-April 1, 2017, April 1 UTC. The municipality's risk assessment records 336 deaths and more than 400 injuries.
sources: Colombia National Disaster Risk Management Unit

title: Garissa University College attack
description: Al-Shabaab gunmen attacked Garissa University College at dawn on April 2, 2015, shooting students and taking hostages. Kenya's interior minister subsequently reported 148 people killed, most of them students. Security forces ended the siege that day.

title: Khan Sheikhoun chemical attack
description: Sarin was used as a chemical weapon at Khan Shaykhun, Syria, on April 4, 2017. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism attributed responsibility to the Syrian Arab Republic. The OPCW fact-finding team identified approximately 100 fatalities but could not establish an exact total.

review.note: OPCW confirms sarin use on April 4, and the JIM attributes responsibility to the Syrian Arab Republic. Do not confuse the FFM's chemical identification remit with JIM's attribution remit. FFM paragraphs 5.80 and 6.13 describe approximately 100 fatalities after potential duplicates among 107 reported names, explicitly unable to determine exact numbers; this does not verify 89 or over 500 distinct injured. The exact toll remains unresolved, independently of the supported attack attribution.

sources.name: OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism report S/2017/904
US Department of State, JIM report summary

title: Battle for Tripoli (Western Libya offensive)
description: On 4 April 2019, forces of the Libyan National Army under Khalifa Haftar launched an offensive to capture Tripoli from the UN-backed Government of National Accord, setting off nearly 14 months of fighting in the capital's southern suburbs. By the end of 2019 the United Nations reported that more than 1,000 people had been killed and about 146,000 displaced, with civilian infrastructure including hospitals and residential areas hit by airstrikes and shelling. The campaign continued into 2020, when a ceasefire and UN-brokered political talks brought a halt to the offensive.

review.note: 1,000 is an interim toll. The offensive ended through military withdrawal in June, before the later ceasefire; final death count remains unresolved.

title: Douma chemical weapons attack
description: On April 7, 2018, a chemical attack in Douma, Syria, killed 43 named people. In January 2023, the OPCW investigation team found reasonable grounds to believe that Syrian air forces dropped two cylinders containing chlorine on residential buildings, affecting dozens more people.

title: Palm Sunday church bombings, Egypt
description: Suicide bombings struck Coptic churches in Tanta and Alexandria on Palm Sunday, April 9, 2017. Islamic State claimed responsibility. The victim toll subsequently reached 47.

title: Kumamoto earthquakes
description: A sequence of earthquakes struck Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan, beginning on April 14, 2016. The larger shock occurred at 16:25 UTC on April 15, April 16 locally. The prefecture records 50 direct deaths and 225 disaster-related deaths; the numeric toll here counts direct deaths only.

title: Ecuador earthquake (M7.8)
description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck coastal Ecuador at 23:58 UTC on April 16, 2016, severely affecting the Pedernales area of Manabi Province. Ecuador's later national planning account reports 676 deaths and more than 16,600 injuries from the disaster.
sources: Ecuador national planning authority, Zone 4 agenda

title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings
description: On Easter Sunday, 21 April 2019, a series of coordinated suicide bombings struck three churches and three luxury hotels in Colombo, Negombo and Batticaloa, with two further explosions occurring later in the day. A total of 269 people were killed, including dozens of foreign nationals, and more than 500 were injured, making it the deadliest act of violence in Sri Lanka since the end of the civil war. The Islamic State claimed responsibility, and investigations focused on the local group National Thowheeth Jama'ath and its links to international militant networks.

review.note: Date and coordinated church/hotel attack supported. 269 excluding nine bombers is in secondary summaries, while initial official counts were sharply revised. Need primary/reputable final total and confirmation of all location/injury/attribution details; do not substitute the preliminary 359 or 250-260.

title: Kabul voter registration center bombing
description: A suicide bomber attacked a voter registration center in the Dasht-e-Barchi district of western Kabul, a predominantly Shia Hazara area, during Afghanistan's parliamentary election registration process. The blast killed at least 57 people and wounded more than 100, mostly civilians queued to obtain voter cards. The Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility for the attack, one of a series targeting the 2018 election process.

review.note: 57 was an initial toll. Later reporting gives more than 60, with secondary summaries giving 69; UNAMA records 198 total civilian casualties without a fatality breakdown in the retrieved page. Exact final death count and breakdown remain unresolved; date, registration-site identity and IS attribution are supported.

title: Nepal earthquake (Gorkha)
description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck central Nepal on April 25, 2015, causing catastrophic building damage, landslides and avalanches. USGS's 2015 summary attributes 8,964 deaths to the disaster, citing OCHA. The toll's treatment of later aftershocks needs reconciliation with separately listed events.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

review.note: USGS attributes 8,964 deaths to the April event citing OCHA, and discusses a sequence including later aftershocks. Country decomposition in original is not confirmed, and separate May 12 row risks double counting. April 25 11:56 local is 06:11 UTC.

title: Idlib offensive (Syria)
description: On 30 April 2019, the Syrian government, backed by Russian air power, launched a ground offensive against opposition-held areas of Idlib Governorate, the last major rebel stronghold. Between April and August, the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights recorded at least 1,043 civilian deaths and roughly 3,000 combatant deaths, while the United Nations reported more than 500 civilians killed in the first months and hundreds of thousands of people displaced, including repeated attacks on schools, hospitals and camps for displaced people.

review.note: Search supports campaign identity and reports 1,043 civilians in secondary coverage. Need the underlying SOHR final interval and combatant total, UN source for 500 deaths, and distinction between April air campaign and subsequent ground offensive. Not verified from secondary summaries.

title: Nepal earthquake aftershock
description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck east of Kathmandu on May 12, 2015, following the April 25 Gorkha earthquake. It caused additional deaths and destruction in Nepal and neighbouring countries. Its separate fatality count must be distinguished from cumulative totals for the earthquake sequence.

review.note: Magnitude/date supported; 218 combines 153 Nepal, 62 India, two Bangladesh and one China in secondary accounting, not 218 in Nepal. Primary country totals and exclusion from April cumulative toll are not established.

title: Gaza border protest killings
description: Israeli forces killed 60 Palestinians during demonstrations near the Gaza perimeter fence on May 14, 2018. A subsequent UN inquiry reported more than 1,100 people shot that day. Across demonstrations from March 30 through December 31, 2018, the inquiry recorded 189 Palestinian deaths, including 183 caused by live ammunition.

title: Cubana de Aviación Flight 972 crash
description: On May 18, 2018, a Boeing 737 operating for Cubana de Aviacion crashed into a field shortly after departing Havana's Jose Marti International Airport. Of the 113 people aboard, 112 died and one survived. The aircraft was operated by Mexican charter company Global Air.

title: Manchester Arena bombing
description: Salman Abedi detonated a suicide bomb at Manchester Arena as an Ariana Grande concert ended on May 22, 2017. Twenty-two victims were killed, excluding the bomber. His brother Hashem was later convicted of helping plan and prepare the attack.
sources: Greater Manchester Police, Hashem Abedi conviction

title: Indian heat wave
location: India, particularly Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
description: Extreme heat affected India during May and early June 2015, with particularly severe mortality in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Contemporary estimates exceeded 2,000 deaths, while surveillance totals differed in coverage. A precise onset date and reconciled death toll remain unestablished.

review.note: May 26 is a reporting-period date, not established onset. NOAA says at least 2,300; NASA cites 2,500 reporting, while national surveillance records a lower figure under different reporting coverage. Resolve onset, death definition and countrywide scope; do not preserve Andhra Pradesh as entire location.

title: Volcán de Fuego eruption
description: Guatemala's Volcán de Fuego erupted violently, sending pyroclastic flows and ash that buried the villages of San Miguel Los Lotes and El Rodeo in mud and rock. The eruption killed 425 people according to Guatemala's disaster agency (CONRED), injured hundreds, destroyed thousands of homes, and forced the evacuation of over 12,000 people, while dozens of victims were never recovered from the deposits.

review.note: June 3 eruption is established. The asserted 425 confirmed CONRED deaths is not established: reports variously combine recovered deaths and missing people, and the 2026 government-newspaper retrospective itself gives 429 dead plus 229 missing. Hundreds injured/thousands of homes destroyed also need final evidence. No numerical replacement proposed without reconciling categories.

title: Khartoum massacre
description: On 3 June 2019, Sudanese security forces, including the Rapid Support Forces, violently dispersed a civilian sit-in outside the army headquarters in Khartoum that had been demanding a transition to civilian rule. The Sudanese Doctors' Syndicate documented at least 104 deaths, with later tallies exceeding 128 including children, and hundreds of people wounded; an official inquiry reported 87 deaths. The crackdown followed the ouster of President Omar al-Bashir and preceded a power-sharing agreement that established a civilian-led transitional government later that year.

review.note: June 3 attack and RSF involvement supported. Amnesty distinguishes at least 100 in its estimate, 127 from Central Committee of Sudanese Doctors, 50 from a different doctors' syndicate, and 87 from attorney-general inquiry. Original 104/128 attribution conflates organizations and reporting intervals; exact canonical tally remains unresolved.

title: Orlando Pulse nightclub shooting
description: A gunman attacked Pulse nightclub in Orlando in the early hours of June 12, 2016, killing 49 victims. The shooting became a hostage incident before police killed the attacker later that morning.

title: Grenfell Tower fire
description: A fire in a fourth-floor flat at Grenfell Tower in London spread through the building's combustible exterior cladding, killing 72 people. It was reported shortly before midnight UTC on June 13, 2017, June 14 locally.

title: Charleston church shooting
description: Dylann Roof killed nine Black worshippers during a Bible study at Emanuel AME Church in Charleston on the evening of June 17, 2015, local time, or June 18 UTC. He was arrested the next day and later convicted on federal hate-crime charges and sentenced to death.

title: Karachi heat wave
description: A severe heatwave struck Karachi and other parts of Sindh in June 2015 during Ramadan. Karachi reached 44.8 C on June 20, and hospitals faced large numbers of heat-related patients. Death estimates changed rapidly and must distinguish the city from provincial or nationwide totals.

review.note: Heatwave predates June 24; PMD identifies June 19-23 and a Karachi maximum 44.8 C June 20. 49 C should not be attributed to Karachi. Neither final city toll 1,265 nor national 2,000 is established by these sources; original poverty and utilities attribution too categorical.

title: Sousse beach attack
description: A gunman attacked holidaymakers at the Imperial Marhaba hotel and beach at Port El Kantaoui near Sousse, Tunisia, shortly before midday on June 26, 2015. Thirty-eight victims were killed, including 30 British citizens.

review.note: Police confirms June 26 shortly before midday, 38 victims including 30 British. Remove unverified exact injury count and superlative; 38 excludes attacker. Midday Tunisia date unchanged UTC. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

sources.name: UK National Police Chiefs' Council, commemoration

title: Atatürk Airport attack
description: Three suicide attackers struck Istanbul's Ataturk Airport on June 28, 2016. Forty-five victims were killed, excluding the three attackers.

title: European heat waves
description: Record-breaking heat waves struck western Europe in late June and late July 2019, with France registering its highest-ever temperature of 45.9°C at Gallargues-le-Montueux on 28 June. France's public health agency attributed 1,435 excess deaths to the June heat wave, and a subsequent peer-reviewed study estimated roughly 2,500 deaths across Europe attributable to the summer's heat waves. Schools closed, rail services were suspended and cities opened cooling centres as authorities issued the highest heat alerts for the first time in several countries.

review.note: Confirmed national record is 46.0 C at Verargues June 28, not 45.9 C at Gallargues. The French mortality bulletin covers both June and July heatwaves. No identifiable peer-reviewed study supporting the claimed Europe-wide 2,500 total retrieved; replacement death scope must be settled before integration.

title: Yemen famine and cholera crisis
description: The war-ravaged country faced the world's worst humanitarian crisis in 2018: UN agencies reported 8.4 million people one step away from famine and over 22 million in need of assistance, while a massive cholera outbreak killed at least 2,315 people out of more than 1.1 million suspected cases recorded since the epidemic began in 2017. Port restrictions, collapsed health infrastructure, and food insecurity compounded the crisis, with the UN warning that parts of the country could slip into famine.

review.note: The outbreak and humanitarian crisis are established, but July 1 is not established as an event or reporting cutoff. The 2,315 total needs its exact WHO reporting interval; this is a cumulative cholera figure, not famine deaths or deaths on July 1. The outbreak began in 2016, with a major wave in April 2017.

title: India monsoon floods
description: The 2019 southwest monsoon caused severe and prolonged flooding across much of India between June and October, with more than 1,600 people killed in rain-related incidents according to reports citing official data. Bihar was among the hardest-hit states, along with Maharashtra, Kerala, Karnataka and Assam, and heavy flooding in the south coincided with torrential rain in Maharashtra's coastal districts. More than a million people were displaced, crops were destroyed and the floods followed unusually heavy August rainfall that came within weeks of drought in parts of the country.

review.note: Reuters supports more than 1,600 rain-related deaths since June by October 1, 2019, not deaths on July 1. Seasonal date anchor and displacement/geographic/detail claims remain incompletely supported. Needs a reporting cutoff rather than single-day presentation. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

title: Majiya fuel tanker explosion
description: In early July 2019, a fuel tanker that had overturned near the village of Majiya in Jigawa State exploded, killing at least 48 people, many of whom had gathered to collect leaking fuel, and leaving dozens more hospitalised with severe burns. Local officials said most of the dead were burnt beyond recognition and the explosion also destroyed nearby properties. The incident highlighted the recurring danger of fuel collection at tanker crash sites across Nigeria, where fuel shortages have driven people to scoop up spilled petrol.

review.note: Search did not establish a July 2019 Majiya explosion killing 48. Primary investigation notice and AFP locate the major Majiya disaster on October 15, 2024 with much higher deaths. Likely conflation, but failed search alone is not proof of fabrication. Quarantine pending identity/date resolution; do not silently repurpose as 2024.

title: Karrada shopping district bombing
description: An Islamic State-claimed suicide bombing devastated Baghdad's Karrada shopping district shortly after midnight locally on July 3, 2016. Later reports attributed differing tolls of 323 and 324 to Iraqi authorities, after much lower preliminary counts.

review.note: Rudaw attributes 324 to the health minister on July 31, while same-period AFP reporting gives 323; both exceed the early 250/292 counts. The attack occurred shortly after midnight July 3 local time, meaning July 2 UTC; exact timing currently has only a tertiary source here. Later tertiary totals and a minister's reported much higher estimate also prevent treating 324 as an uncontested final toll. Proposed UTC shift requires stronger timing corroboration before publication.

title: 2016 China floods (Yangtze basin)
description: Torrential monsoon rains produced the worst flooding in China since 1998, hitting the Yangtze and Huai river basins across 26 provinces and affecting an estimated 32 million people, with hundreds of thousands left homeless. More than 350 people died in the floods, and a June 23 EF4 tornado in Jiangsu Province that killed at least 99 people brought the combined toll to more than 440. Rivers breached their banks in multiple provinces, including Hubei and Anhui, and damage was estimated in the tens of billions of dollars.

review.note: July 5 is a reporting date, not an established onset of the June-September flood season. The 449 total combines more than 350 flood deaths with 99 deaths in the separate June 23 Jiangsu tornado, inconsistent with the Yangtze flood title. TIME's July 5 report gives 186 dead and 45 missing as of the preceding Sunday, a preliminary count, not support for 449 flood deaths. Define flood period and geography before selecting date or final toll.

title: Western Japan floods and landslides
description: Heavy rainfall from late June through early July 2018 caused flooding and landslides across western Japan, especially Hiroshima, Okayama and Ehime. A published mortality analysis recorded 237 deaths, including 115 in Hiroshima Prefecture. The July 6 calendar entry falls within the multi-day disaster.

review.note: 225 is an early reported tally; published mortality analysis gives 237. JMA documents June 28-July 8 rainfall, including cumulative totals over 1,800 mm, not the asserted 180 mm/hour. July 6 is an anchor within the disaster, not all deaths on that date. The precise July 6 calendar date remains an unestablished selection within a June 28-July 8 rainfall episode; explaining it as an anchor does not verify it as the event date.

title: Dallas police ambush
description: A gunman attacked police during a protest in Dallas on the evening of July 7, 2016, July 8 UTC. Five officers were killed and nine officers were wounded.

title: Victory declared in Mosul
description: Iraq declared victory over Islamic State in Mosul on July 10, 2017, while some fighting continued. An Associated Press investigation estimated 9,000-11,000 civilian deaths in the campaign from October 2016 to July 2017. The numeric toll is an approximate midpoint of that estimate.
sources: PBS interview with Associated Press investigator

title: Mastung election rally bombing
description: A suicide bomber attacked a Balochistan Awami Party election rally near Mastung, Pakistan, on July 13, 2018. A subsequent official tally reported by Reuters put the deaths at 149, including candidate Siraj Raisani. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

title: Nice Bastille Day truck attack
description: A truck was driven into crowds celebrating Bastille Day on Nice's Promenade des Anglais on July 14, 2016. Eighty-six people were killed and hundreds were injured. Police killed the driver.

title: Attempted coup in Turkey
description: A faction of Turkey's armed forces attempted to overthrow the government on the night of July 15, 2016, with violence in Ankara and Istanbul. The attempt failed. Later official commemorations count 251 people killed opposing the coup, a narrower scope than totals including coup participants.

review.note: July 15-16 attempted coup in Ankara and Istanbul is supported. Later Turkish commemoration counts 251 people killed opposing the coup, excluding coup participants; HRW reported at least 241 citizens/security personnel earlier. Neither establishes a consistently scoped combined toll of 300 or the claimed 180 civilians. Later injury counts also vary. Keep the core toll unresolved rather than silently substitute a loyalist-only count.

title: Munich Olympia shopping mall shooting
description: A gunman killed nine people at and near Munich's Olympia shopping centre on July 22, 2016, before killing himself. The city officially commemorates the attack as racist and right-wing terrorism. The toll excludes the attacker.

title: Kabul twin bombing of Hazara demonstration
description: Two suicide bombers attacked a peaceful demonstration at Kabul's Deh Mazang square on July 23, 2016. UNAMA documented 85 civilian deaths and 413 injuries. Islamic State's local affiliate claimed responsibility.
sources: UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan, 2016 annual civilian protection report

title: El Paso Walmart shooting
description: A gunman targeting Hispanic shoppers attacked the Cielo Vista Walmart in El Paso, Texas, on August 3, 2019. Twenty-three people died and 22 were injured. The attacker pleaded guilty to federal hate-crime and firearms charges and was sentenced in July 2023 to 90 consecutive life terms.

title: Lombok earthquake sequence
description: A series of major earthquakes struck the island of Lombok between July 29 and August 19, 2018, the strongest being a magnitude 7.0 quake on August 5. The quakes destroyed more than 70,000 homes, triggered landslides on Mount Rinjani, and killed at least 563 people, including tourists in the Gili Islands, with over 1,000 injured and roughly 350,000 displaced.

review.note: August 5 date and magnitude 7.0 per Indonesian authority supported. 563 is a sequence-wide figure in secondary accounts. Need final BNPB report for death, housing and displacement totals and especially purported tourist deaths in the Gili Islands; sources retrieved do not establish those full-record details.

title: Saada school bus airstrike
description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a school bus at Dahyan market in Saada Governorate on August 9, 2018. The ICRC relayed a local-authority tally of 51 dead, including 40 children, and 79 injured.

title: Tianjin warehouse explosions
description: A fire and explosions at a hazardous-goods warehouse in Tianjin on August 12, 2015, killed 165 people, with eight others missing, according to the official investigation. Another 798 were hospitalized. Investigators traced the fire to nitrocellulose that had dried and self-heated.

review.note: Official investigation distinguishes 165 confirmed dead plus eight missing, including five missing port firefighters. Thus 173 and 104 firefighters include missing presumed dead. Proposed count is confirmed-only; remove unverified explosive quantities. Late night August 12 local remains August 12 UTC. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

title: Freetown mudslide and floods, Sierra Leone
description: A major landslide entered the Babadorie River valley near Freetown on August 14, 2017, worsening widespread flooding. The World Bank assessment records about 6,000 people affected across the Western Area and 1,141 declared dead or missing, without equating all missing people with confirmed deaths.

review.note: The August 14 landslide and flooding are supported, but 1,141 explicitly combines dead and missing, not confirmed deaths. The assessment concerns the wider Western Area disaster, not solely Regent. No reconciled confirmed-death total was established here. Remove unsupported orphan and displacement counts while retaining the documented affected scope.

sources.name: World Bank damage and loss assessment

title: Kerala floods
description: Monsoon flooding and landslides devastated Kerala in August 2018. A case study hosted by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority reports over 483 deaths and about one million evacuees, with 35 dams opened. Other assessments use different reporting intervals and totals; these deaths did not all occur on August 15.

review.note: Over 100 dams is wrong: state-hosted case study gives 35, UNDP 37. Report intervals produce 433 versus 483 deaths. Preserve 483 only as the broader case-study tally and make multi-day scope clear. The precise August 15 calendar anchor remains unestablished within the multi-day flood period; retain the supported prose correction but withhold until the date/period representation is resolved.

title: Central Italy earthquake (Amatrice)
description: A magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck central Italy at 01:36 UTC on August 24, 2016. Italy's Civil Protection Department records 299 deaths: 237 in Amatrice, 11 in Accumoli and 51 in Arquata del Tronto.
sources: Italian Civil Protection Department, August 2018 update

title: Rohingya clearance operations, Myanmar
description: Myanmar's military launched clearance operations against Rohingya communities in Rakhine State on August 25, 2017. MSF's refugee surveys estimated that at least 6,700 Rohingya died violently between August 25 and September 24, including at least 730 children under five. The numeric toll represents that first-month estimate.

title: South Asia floods
description: Monsoon flooding affected Bangladesh, India and Nepal in August 2017. On September 2, UNICEF reported at least 1,288 deaths since mid-August and estimated more than 45 million people affected. Affected population is not the same as displaced population.

review.note: UNICEF's September 2 release supports at least 1,288 reported deaths since mid-August and over 45 million affected, not 40 million displaced. August 28 is an unsupported single-day anchor within an ongoing monsoon disaster. The toll is a dated preliminary count, not a reconciled season total; do not replace the date with the publication date and call it verified.

title: Typhoon Lionrock floods in North Korea
description: Heavy rain associated with Typhoon Lionrock caused severe flooding in northeastern North Korea in late August 2016. A September 14 UN update reported 138 confirmed deaths and 400 people missing. Those missing were not confirmed dead in that report.

review.note: The September 11 UN report lists 133 confirmed dead and 395 missing; September 14 gives 138 and 400. Neither supports more than 500 confirmed deaths in North Korea or 550 internationally. Missing people cannot simply be added to confirmed deaths. OCHA references August 29 while ACAPS describes August 30; Japan landfall does not establish North Korea's flood onset or its UTC date. Core date and final toll remain unresolved.

sources.name: United Nations in DPR Korea, September 11 update
United Nations in DPR Korea, September 14 update

title: Hurricane Dorian
location: Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama, Bahamas
description: Hurricane Dorian, a Category 5 storm with sustained winds of 185 mph, devastated the northern Bahamas when it made landfall on 1 September 2019, stalling over the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama for more than a day. The storm killed 84 people across all affected areas, including 74 in the Bahamas, where hundreds of people were initially reported missing and whole settlements were flattened by the storm surge. It was the strongest hurricane on record to hit the Bahamas and caused tens of thousands of people to be displaced or left homeless.

review.note: September 1 landfall, category 5 and 185 mph established. Need reconcile 84 all-area deaths and 74 Bahamas with NHC confirmed/reported and missing categories and later Bahamas revisions; no full verification of numeric death/displacement scope. The NHC report could not be opened successfully (access denied), so its final mortality table was not checked.

title: Chiapas earthquake, Mexico
description: A magnitude 8.2 earthquake struck offshore Chiapas, Mexico, at 04:49 UTC on September 8, 2017, late September 7 locally. The disaster killed at least 98 people and caused extensive damage in southern Mexico.

title: Mecca crane collapse
description: A crawler crane collapsed onto Mecca's Grand Mosque during a severe storm on the late afternoon of September 11, 2015, killing 111 people and injuring 394. Manufacturer Liebherr said the crane was caught by strong winds and should have been placed in its prescribed storm configuration.
sources: Florida Building Commission, engineering review draft

title: Typhoon Mangkhut
description: Typhoon Mangkhut, the strongest storm of the year, made landfall in northern Luzon, Philippines, on September 15, 2018, with sustained winds of 205 km/h. The typhoon triggered landslides in mining and farming areas, destroyed over 400,000 homes, and killed at least 134 people in the Philippines, with additional deaths reported in Hong Kong and southern China. Storm surges and flooding affected millions across the region.

review.note: Landfall was early September 15 local time, September 14 UTC; UTC date correction supported. 134 is a multinational total in secondary summaries, not Philippine deaths; Hong Kong deaths and 400,000 destroyed homes are not substantiated. Keep unresolved until a consistent final geographic toll and damage definition are established.

title: Puebla earthquake, Mexico
location: Puebla, Morelos and Mexico City, Mexico
description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck central Mexico on September 19, 2017, damaging Puebla, Morelos and Mexico City. Mexico's CENAPRED records 369 deaths. The quake occurred on the anniversary of the 1985 Mexico City earthquake.

title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico
description: Hurricane Maria made landfall in Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, as a Category 4 hurricane with sustained winds of 155 mph. A George Washington University study estimated 2,975 excess deaths from September 2017 through February 2018 after accounting for population displacement. This is a modeled estimate, not a count of individually certified storm deaths.
sources: US National Weather Service, San Juan

title: MV Nyerere ferry capsizing
description: The overloaded ferry MV Nyerere capsized while approaching Ukara Island on Lake Victoria on September 20, 2018. Later government figures put the death toll at 228, with 41 people rescued. It had been travelling from Ukerewe Island.

review.note: Ferry was approaching Ukara, not just departing Ukerewe. 41 survivors, not hundreds; 228 is the later government tally summarized by secondary source, while September 24 AFP still reported 224. The later 228 toll was not corroborated beyond a secondary summary in this batch; the opened contemporary AFP source still had 224. Route/survivor corrections do not establish a final death tally.

title: Sulawesi earthquake and tsunami
description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, triggering a tsunami up to six meters high that hit Palu Bay, along with widespread soil liquefaction that swallowed entire neighborhoods. The disaster destroyed tens of thousands of buildings in Palu, Donggala, and Sigi and displaced over 200,000 people. Indonesia's disaster agency (BNPB) confirmed 4,340 deaths, more than 10,000 injured, and hundreds missing.

review.note: Date, magnitude and disaster identity supported. Need reconcile 4,340 with recovered bodies, missing and people presumed buried; calling all confirmed deaths while also listing missing risks category mixing. BNPB page returned 403 on open. Tsunami-height maximum and displacement total also require final source.

title: Kunduz hospital airstrike
description: A US AC-130 attacked MSF's Kunduz trauma hospital early on October 3, 2015, local time, or October 2 UTC. MSF confirmed at least 42 deaths: 14 staff, 24 patients and four caretakers. The US military described the strike as mistaken and administratively disciplined 16 personnel; none faced court-martial.

title: Las Vegas Route 91 Harvest festival shooting
description: A gunman fired from the Mandalay Bay hotel into the Route 91 Harvest festival crowd on the Las Vegas Strip late on October 1, 2017, October 2 UTC. The official toll is 60 victims, including two who died from their injuries in 2019 and 2020, and excludes the attacker.
sources: Federal Bureau of Investigation, incident chronology
Las Vegas Review-Journal, official revised toll

title: Hurricane Matthew in Haiti
description: Hurricane Matthew struck southwestern Haiti on October 4, 2016, as a Category 4 hurricane. The post-disaster assessment records 546 deaths in Haiti and 128 people missing. The numeric toll counts confirmed Haitian deaths, not missing people or deaths in other countries.
sources: International Labour Organization, Haiti post-disaster needs assessment
United Nations Haiti humanitarian response plan

title: Yemen wedding party airstrike
description: A wedding gathering near Mokha, Yemen, was struck on September 28, 2015. Residents attributed it to the Saudi-led coalition, which denied involvement. Contemporary reporting put deaths at 131, while a UN panel later cited at least 135. This was distinct from the October 2015 Sanaban wedding attack and the October 2016 Sanaa funeral strike.

review.note: Conflation: Mokha wedding was September 28; Sanaban wedding was October 7; acknowledged October 8 strike concerns Sanaa funeral in 2016. Mokha reports 131 versus UN panel at least135; coalition denied responsibility. Supported local calendar correction supplied, but precise UTC time and final toll unresolved.

title: Sanaa funeral hall airstrike
description: Saudi-led coalition airstrikes hit a funeral ceremony in Sanaa on October 8, 2016. The coalition initially denied responsibility before acknowledging the attack. Reported casualty counts differed and were preliminary.

review.note: October 8 funeral attack and coalition responsibility are supported; HRW documents the initial denial and subsequent acknowledgement. The 155 figure was explicitly preliminary in same-day reporting. UN initially reported over 140, while HRW later cited the health ministry's at least 110/610, with identification incomplete. No reconciled final 155/525 tally is established. Preserve this contradiction, not a definitive replacement death count.

title: Ankara peace rally bombing
description: Two suicide bombers attacked a peace-rally gathering outside Ankara's central railway station on October 10, 2015. The toll rose to 103 in November 2015; later commemorative accounts differ on whether 103 or 104 victims are counted. Islamic State was identified as responsible.

review.note: 102 superseded by103 in November2015; 2025 accounts still differ103/104. The record's109 is not reconciled with these sources. Morning October10 date sound; final fatality definition and later deaths unresolved.

title: Typhoon Hagibis
description: Typhoon Hagibis, one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in decades, made landfall on the Izu Peninsula near Tokyo on 12 October 2019, bringing record rainfall that caused more than 70 rivers to overflow and widespread landslides. Around 100 people were killed, more than 350 were injured and thousands of homes were flooded, with several prefectures including Nagano, Fukushima and Miyagi among the worst affected. The storm disrupted transport, power and the 2019 Rugby World Cup, and the government described the scale of damage as unprecedented.

review.note: Government white paper gives 91 dead, three missing, 42 seriously and 334 lightly injured as of April 10, 2020. About 100 may reflect later indirect deaths; source for that basis absent. Need consistent final interval and source for 70 rivers/world-cup/superlative claims. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

title: Mogadishu truck bombing
description: A truck bombing devastated Mogadishu's Zoobe intersection on October 14, 2017. The Zobe Rescue Committee later reported 587 deaths, but a UN monitoring report cites 582 and also notes a separate 587 count. The final toll and scope of the day's separate explosions need reconciliation.

review.note: Hiiraan's March 5 report attributes 587 to the Zobe Rescue Committee of volunteers and officials, not a parliamentary committee. Its final report was released March 4, increasing December's 512. The UN monitoring report gives as many as 582 in its main text and notes ACLED's 587, an unresolved discrepancy. Also distinguish the principal truck blast from the second explosion before assigning a combined toll. Original Hiiraan URL failed to open; an indexed rendering supplied the article text.

sources.name: Hiiraan Online report, accessible archived rendering
UN Somalia Monitoring Group report S/2018/1002

title: End of the Raqqa campaign declared
description: The SDF and US-led coalition operation to capture Raqqa from Islamic State was declared complete on October 17, 2017. A later Amnesty International and Airwars investigation reported more than 1,600 civilians killed by coalition air and artillery strikes during the June-October campaign. That figure is not an all-perpetrator battle total.

review.note: The operation was declared complete October 17 after beginning June 6. Amnesty/Airwars' later investigation reports more than 1,600 civilian deaths from coalition air and artillery strikes, not a 1,300-1,600 airstrike-only range. That source-specific count does not establish the original 1,800 all-perpetrator battle total or reconcile the several local-monitor totals. Keep core toll unresolved; do not create a synthetic midpoint across differently scoped estimates.

title: Siege of Marawi ends
description: Fighting between Philippine forces and Islamic State-aligned militants in Marawi began on May 23, 2017. The government declared the city liberated on October 17 and announced the end of combat operations on October 23. Published casualty breakdowns differ in their inclusion of civilians who died of illness.

review.note: October 23 is the declared end of combat operations; the separate liberation announcement was October 17. The original 1,233 sums 978 militants, 168 government personnel and 87 civilians; tertiary reporting says 40 of those civilians died of illness. The Army-hosted clipping repeats some later numbers but an authoritative reconciled total and direct/indirect scope were not established; the presidential briefing failed to open. Remove the inaccurate only-Muslim-majority-city claim and other ancillary rankings/costs. The exact total remains unresolved.

sources.name: Philippine Presidential Communications Office, October 27 briefing

title: Quetta police training college attack
description: Attackers stormed the police training college near Quetta late on October 24, 2016. Lashkar-e-Jhangvi claimed collaboration with Islamic State in the attack. Published victim counts range above the initially reported 61.

review.note: The Tribune supports the October 24 attack and early 61/165 count. Later Dawn gives 64 including two non-cadet personnel. Australia's listing gives at least 62 and notes LeJ claimed collaboration with Islamic State. The original exact total is not reconciled. Remove the false deadliest-since-2014 ranking: the Lahore Easter bombing in 2016 was deadlier.

title: Hindu Kush earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck Afghanistan's Hindu Kush on October 26, 2015. Reports recorded 280 deaths in Pakistan and 115 in Afghanistan, with widespread damage across both countries. A consistent all-country total remains to be established.

review.note: USGS confirms magnitude7.5 at09:09UTC October26; primary reports support280 Pakistan and115 Afghanistan. Four India deaths and exact399 total not independently established. Do not silently certify whole regional sum.

title: Pittsburgh synagogue shooting
description: An antisemitic gunman attacked worshippers at Pittsburgh's Tree of Life synagogue on October 27, 2018, killing 11 people from three congregations during Shabbat services. Six others, including four police officers, were wounded. It was the deadliest antisemitic attack in United States history.

title: Lion Air Flight 610 crash
description: Lion Air Flight 610, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 travelling from Jakarta to Pangkal Pinang, crashed into the Java Sea about 13 minutes after takeoff, killing all 189 aboard. It was early October 29, 2018 locally, still October 28 UTC. Investigators documented technical problems on preceding flights.

title: Metrojet Flight 9268 bombing
description: Metrojet Flight 9268 broke up over Egypt's Sinai Peninsula on October 31, 2015, killing all 224 people aboard the Sharm el-Sheikh-Saint Petersburg flight. Islamic State claimed responsibility. Russian authorities concluded a bomb destroyed the aircraft, and Egypt's president later acknowledged terrorism caused the crash.

title: Tezgam train fire
description: The Karachi-to-Rawalpindi Tezgam Express caught fire near Rahim Yar Khan at about 06:30 local time on October 31, 2019. Radio Pakistan reported 74 deaths that day. Later inquiry reporting identified a possible electrical short circuit followed by cylinder explosions.

title: Sutherland Springs church shooting
description: A gunman attacked First Baptist Church in Sutherland Springs, Texas, on November 5, 2017. Authorities count 26 victims, including the unborn child of a pregnant woman who was killed, and 22 injured. The victim toll excludes the attacker.
sources: US Department of Justice, event date

title: Camp Fire wildfire
description: The Camp Fire began in Butte County, California, on November 8, 2018 and devastated Paradise and nearby communities. It killed 85 people, burned 153,336 acres and destroyed 18,804 structures.

title: Beirut suicide bombings
description: Two suicide bombings struck the crowded Bourj el-Barajneh area in Beirut's southern suburbs on November 12, 2015. At least 43 people were reported killed and more than 240 wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

title: Iran-Iraq earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck near the Iran-Iraq border on November 12, 2017. It killed approximately 630 people and caused severe damage, particularly around Sarpol-e Zahab in Iran. The numeric toll is approximate.

title: Paris Attacks
description: Coordinated shootings and suicide bombings struck Paris and Saint-Denis on November 13, 2015, including the Bataclan, restaurants and Stade de France. They killed 130 people in the immediate attacks and injured more than 400. France's later official toll is 132, including two survivors who subsequently died by suicide.

title: Bir al-Abed mosque attack, Egypt
location: Al-Rawda near Bir al-Abed, North Sinai, Egypt
description: Armed attackers struck al-Rawda mosque near Bir al-Abed in North Sinai during Friday prayers on November 24, 2017. Later reports put the death toll at 311. The mosque is associated with a Sufi community.
sources: Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy

title: Chennai floods
description: Repeated northeast-monsoon rains flooded Chennai and other parts of Tamil Nadu in November-December 2015. Official and research accounts give differing death totals for the city, state and wider region. The final severe flooding followed early-December rain, but losses accumulated over a longer period.

review.note: 500 is broader South India estimate,422 appears in NIDM,470 is statewide monsoon count. December1 does not represent the whole November-December episode. Resolve period and geography before assigning a count/date. NGO CAG differs from Comptroller and Auditor General.

sources.name: NITI Aayog, Tamil Nadu flood review
Citizen consumer and civic Action Group, assessment

title: San Bernardino shooting
description: Two attackers opened fire at a San Bernardino County employee gathering at the Inland Regional Center on December 2, 2015, killing 14 people and injuring 22 according to the county's retrospective. The FBI classified it as terrorism. Both attackers were killed in a later confrontation with police.

title: Whakaari/White Island eruption
location: Whakaari/White Island, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand
description: Whakaari/White Island erupted in New Zealand's Bay of Plenty on December 9, 2019, while visitors and guides were on the island. Twenty-two people died and 25 were injured, most critically. Two victims' bodies were not recovered.

title: Mogadishu truck bombing
description: On 28 December 2019, a truck bomb detonated at the Ex-Control Afgoye checkpoint on the outskirts of Mogadishu, followed by another blast at a bus station in the city, killing at least 85 people and injuring more than 140. The attack hit taxis, buses and minibuses collecting passengers at the checkpoint during rush hour, and al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. It was among the deadliest attacks in Mogadishu in years and targeted a route frequented by civilians travelling between the capital and surrounding towns.

review.note: 85 appears in later secondary totals. A second bus-station blast is not established and may conflate a different bombing. Need final reputable toll and responsibility statement.
